drhp.business: IMIL designs and manufactures precision actuator DC motors and motor sub-assemblies for automotive applications, supplying global and domestic Tier-1 suppliers and OEMs. Its automotive range began with Electronic Throttle Control within Engine Air Management and has extended into safety-critical applications (EPB, PLA, GBA, ABS) and body applications (TOCD, seat motors, HRA). Alongside automotive, it makes energy-efficient BLDC motors and driver electronics (ESDM) for the electrical consumer durables / FMEG segment, having entered BLDC ceiling fan motors in 2020.

risks.note: Igarashi operates in a dynamic global environment where geo-political developments, changing tariff regimes, trade policy and tariff uncertainties, inflationary pressures, energy crisis and fluctuations in global automotive demand may impact export business and supply chains; mitigation is through diversifying the customer base and export markets, local-for-local supply chain resilience and close monitoring of regulatory developments.
risks.risk: Macro risks and strategic foresight - geo-political developments, changing tariff regimes and trade policy uncertainty

risks.note: Rapid transition towards vehicle electrification, advanced mobility solutions and evolving customer requirements necessitates continuous product innovation; the Company channels resources into R&D to strengthen BLDC motor technologies and develop motor solutions for next-generation mobility.

Increasing global competition, pricing pressure, localization requirements and evolving customer sourcing strategies influence market dynamics; addressed by engineering expertise, cost competitiveness, supply-chain re-alignment and expanding presence across global OEMs, new applications and export markets.
risks.risk: Market dynamics and competitive edge - pricing pressure and localization requirements

risks.note: Rigorous quality benchmarks, intricate supply chain dynamics, raw material price volatility, logistics challenges and workforce adaptation alongside advancing automation; mitigated by strengthening supply chain durability, digital manufacturing and upgrading employee capabilities including FMEA and system validation.
risks.risk: Operational excellence and agility - quality benchmarks, supply chain complexity and raw material volatility

risks.note: Foreign exchange fluctuations, commodity price volatility, interest rate movements and changing global economic conditions may affect financial performance; managed through hedging protocols overseen by the Audit Committee, commodity price pass-through arrangements, working capital optimisation and flexible capital allocation.
risks.risk: Financial stability and risk hedging - forex, commodity and interest rate exposure

risks.note: Escalating cyber risks, data protection challenges and evolving regulatory requirements for personal data; addressed with robust IT controls, periodic vulnerability assessments, employee awareness programmes and continuous real-time monitoring of critical systems.

Environmental regulations, customer sustainability expectations and workplace safety and welfare requirements continue to shape business operations; addressed through energy-efficient operations, responsible resource management, an ESG-compliant supply chain system and regulatory compliance.
risks.risk: Sustainability and ESG leadership - environmental regulation and customer sustainability expectations

risks.note: Extreme weather events due to climate change pose a physical risk of disruption to operations and to the safety of employees; a contingency plan and trained emergency response team members are in place, with property damage capable of halting operations for a limited time.

sk.overview: The industry covers control-intensive, critical-to-the-application electronic control units (ECUs) for the mobility (2/3-wheeler) and industrial (generator/genset) markets. In mobility, ECUs (ISG, EFI, ISG+EFI, EV motor control units) are indispensable to vehicle function; adoption is driven by regulation (emissions/efficiency) and OEM technology transitions, with Tier-I suppliers driving innovation.
